_purpose: Functional scenarios (1 success + technique-driven alternative[]) per acceptance criterion for UC1a. No unit tests. Executable-ready — feeds test cases / automation.
_status: phase-3-3 output — 2026-07-09. Derived from PDT-3562-uc1a-complete-jira-story.json (8 BR / 11 AC) + PDT-3562-uc1a-test-design.md (27 L3 conditions). UC1a = the video / recorded-LS player component. FU-2 RESOLVED (central button hit-target 64x64px) -> the AC-02 pause-vs-dismiss boundary is testable now (SC-UC1a-02). ASSUME-recorded-resume PENDING (Engineering) -> the recorded-LS exact-resume row is held in SC-UC1a-05. The web overlay 3s->1s auto-dismiss is a when-stable regression guard on SC-UC1a-03/08 (iOS already 1s; web when VideoPlayerControls.tsx:60-70 lands).

_rules_applied.split_per_state: AC-11 (app backgrounded, OS default) has TWO valid outcomes by entry state — backgrounded while the overlay was PLAYING -> on foreground the playing overlay is dismissed (its wall-clock 1s idle timer elapsed) and the OS-paused media does not auto-resume; backgrounded while PAUSED -> the paused overlay persists and the media stays paused => SC-UC1a-11a (playing) + SC-UC1a-11b (paused). Every other AC has a single valid outcome -> 1 scenario each. AC-01's mobile-reveal vs desktop-1-Step-Pause difference is PLATFORM variance (BR-09), carried in platform_expected — not a precondition-state split.
_rules_applied.one_owner_per_br: BR-01->AC-04 (SC-04) · BR-03->AC-03 (SC-03) · BR-06->AC-06 (SC-06) · BR-09->AC-01 (SC-01) · BR-10->AC-01 (SC-01) · BR-11->AC-04 (SC-04) · BR-13->AC-05 (SC-05) · BR-15->AC-10 (SC-10). Each cross-cutting rule owned by the single most-direct AC; every other scenario CITES (does not re-assert). AC-01 owns BR-09+BR-10 (first-tap reveal is the headline no-implicit-toggle — the story's core promise). AC-04 owns BR-01+BR-11 (seek-controls-only-on-video/recorded + paused-overlay-persists). BR-11's playing-dismiss branch (AC-02/AC-03/AC-09) and BR-10's dismiss/race/background facets (AC-02/AC-04/AC-09/AC-11) cite, not re-own.

scenarios.title: First tap reveals controls without toggling playback (mobile)
scenarios.automation_note: run BOTH form factors — mobile reveal is the success (Detox iOS/Android · Playwright mobile viewport); desktop (Web UIKit) 1-Step Pause is the platform_expected branch, never reuse the mobile expected on desktop
preconditions: a video or recorded live stream is playing on a mobile surface (iOS / Android / web-on-mobile)
the controls overlay is currently hidden
currentTime is advancing (e.g. at 0:30)
steps: Tap anywhere on the player surface (first tap)
Assert: the controls overlay appears
Assert: playback continues — currentTime keeps advancing, the media does NOT pause (video.paused === false)
Assert: the central button shows the PAUSE icon (reflecting the playing state)

expected.success: On mobile, the first tap on a playing video/recorded LS reveals the controls overlay while playback continues uninterrupted (currentTime keeps advancing, video.paused===false) and the central button shows the PAUSE icon — the tap does not toggle playback.
alternative: On mobile, a first tap that PAUSES the media (currentTime stops / play icon shows) is the wrong class — that is the desktop 1-Step-Pause behaviour (BR-09); on mobile a reveal that toggles playback is the accidental-interrupt regression this story exists to prevent (BR-10).
The overlay must actually appear — a first tap that neither reveals the controls nor pauses (a no-op) is a failure.

platform_expected.note: 1-Step Pause (BR-09 / PV-1): the first click PAUSES directly (currentTime stops, video.paused===true), shows the PLAY icon and the +/-10s skip controls — the mobile reveal branch is NOT taken (TC-UC1a-04b)

scenarios.title: Tap outside the button dismisses the overlay, playback continues
scenarios.automation_note: assert just-inside vs just-outside against the RENDERED 64x64px central button (FU-2 resolved; impl may be the platform-native control)
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
the central pause/play button's rendered hit-target is 64x64px (FU-2 resolved)
steps: Tap the player surface OUTSIDE the central button's 64x64px tap target
Assert: the overlay dismisses
Assert: playback continues uninterrupted — state stays playing (video.paused === false)

expected.success: Tapping outside the 64x64px central button dismisses the overlay while playback continues uninterrupted (state stays playing) — the dismiss is not an implicit pause.
alternative: A tap just INSIDE the rendered 64x64px central button pauses (playing -> paused) instead of dismissing — the pause-vs-dismiss boundary (FU-2 resolved: 64x64px; assert against the rendered target, which may be native).
A tap-outside that transitions playing -> paused is a failure — dismissing the overlay must never implicitly pause the media (BR-10).

scenarios.title: No action for 1s (playing) auto-dismisses the overlay
scenarios.automation_note: when-stable: web overlay 3s->1s regression guard (VideoPlayerControls.tsx:60-70) — iOS/mobile 1s automate now, web when the fix lands; prefer fake-timers / Playwright clock over wall-clock timing
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
no further user interaction occurs
steps: Reveal the overlay while playing, then take no action
Advance the idle timer to 900ms; Assert: the overlay is STILL visible
Advance the idle timer to 1000ms; Assert: the overlay auto-dismisses
Assert: playback continues throughout — currentTime still advancing

expected.success: After exactly 1s (1000ms) of no interaction while playing, the overlay auto-dismisses and playback continues (currentTime still advancing); at 900ms it is still visible.
alternative: At 900ms (just below the 1s bound) the overlay must still be visible — dismissing before 1s is a boundary failure.
The overlay must auto-dismiss at 1000ms, not 3000ms — web currently uses a 3s timer (VideoPlayerControls.tsx:60-70); any dismiss later than 1s fails the regression guard (iOS is already 1s).

scenarios.title: Pause shows play icon + seek controls; paused overlay persists, tap-outside stays paused
scenarios.automation_note: with-mock: SDK stream-type for the recorded-LS (TC-UC1a-01b) and Live-contrast (TC-UC1a-01c) rows; the pause + paused-persist + tap-outside rows are plain local-media Automate
preconditions: a video or recorded live stream is playing with the controls overlay visible
the central button's rendered hit-target is 64x64px (FU-2 resolved)
steps: Tap the central pause button
Assert: playback pauses at the current position (video.paused === true)
Assert: the icon switches pause -> play and the PLAY icon remains visible
Assert: BOTH the -10s AND the +10s skip buttons remain visible (video/recorded component — BR-01)
Advance >1000ms with no interaction; Assert: the overlay PERSISTS (the paused branch has no idle auto-dismiss)
Tap outside the 64x64px central button; Assert: the overlay dismisses AND the media stays paused (does not resume)

expected.success: On a playing video/recorded LS the central pause tap pauses playback at the current position and the play icon persists; the +/-10s seek controls remain visible; while paused the overlay persists past 1s (no idle auto-dismiss); a tap-outside dismisses the overlay and the media stays paused.
alternative: Contrast: on an active Live stream the +/-10s seek controls are NOT shown — proving the seek gate is stream-type driven; seek exists only on video/recorded (BR-01, TC-UC1a-01c).
A paused overlay must NOT auto-dismiss on the 1s idle timer — the paused branch has no idle timeout, so it persists until a tap-outside (BR-11).
A tap-outside while paused must never resume playback — the dismiss is not an implicit play; the media stays paused (BR-10).

platform_expected.note: reaches the paused state via a 1-step pause (BR-09, TC-UC1a-04b) — there is no mobile reveal-then-pause step; once paused the seek-visible / persist / tap-outside-stays-paused behaviour is identical

scenarios.title: Tap play resumes a paused video from the exact position
scenarios.automation_note: with-mock: SDK stream-type for the recorded-LS / Live rows; the recorded-LS exact-resume assertion is HELD (ASSUME-recorded-resume, Engineering) — observe/record, do not assert
preconditions: a video is paused at a known position (t=42s) on a known-length local fixture
the central play button is displayed
steps: Tap the central play button
Assert: playback resumes from currentTime === 42s (not 0, not the live edge)
Assert: the icon switches play -> pause

expected.success: Tapping the central play button on a paused video resumes playback from the exact paused position (t=42s -> resumes at 42s, not 0 and not the live edge); the icon switches play -> pause.
alternative: On a Live stream, resume goes to the current live edge (approx. live within tolerance), NOT the exact paused position — a media-type contrast (BR-13; cross-ref UC2 CONF-07 tolerance).
Recorded LS is ASSUMED to resume from the exact paused position like video — this row is observed/recorded, NOT asserted, until ASSUME-recorded-resume is confirmed by Engineering (TC-UC1a-07b).

pending.note: Only the recorded-LS row (TC-UC1a-07b) is held — do not assert recorded-LS exact-resume until Engineering confirms. The video exact-resume success (TC-UC1a-07a) and the Live-edge contrast (TC-UC1a-07c) are assertable now. If recorded LS instead snaps to the live edge, TC-UC1a-07b flips toward the TC-UC1a-07c expected.

scenarios.title: Reveal behaviour is identical across all in-scope surfaces
scenarios.automation_note: parameterize over the 6 surface classes with the platform held fixed; TC-UC1a-03b runs both form factors to prove surface-invariant != platform-invariant
preconditions: a video or recorded live stream renders on an in-scope surface
the platform (form factor) is held fixed while the surface varies
the 6 in-scope surfaces are available: global / user / community / event-discussion feed, media gallery, fullscreen
steps: For each of the 6 surfaces: perform the AC-01..AC-05 actions (reveal, tap-outside dismiss, 1s auto-dismiss, pause, resume); record the outcomes
Assert: on every surface the outcomes are IDENTICAL — the overlay reveals and playback continues the same way (surface-invariant)

expected.success: The reveal / tap-outside-dismiss / 1s auto-dismiss / pause / resume behaviours produce identical outcomes across all 6 in-scope surfaces {global, user, community, event-discussion feed, media gallery, fullscreen} (surface-invariant).
alternative: Any in-scope surface producing a DIFFERENT reveal / dismiss / auto-dismiss / pause / resume outcome than another in-scope surface is a surface-invariance break (BR-06 violation).

platform_expected.note: surface-invariant != platform-invariant: the same surface on desktop still differs (1-Step Pause, paused, play icon — BR-09) instead of the mobile reveal (playing) — expected platform variance, not a BR-06 break (TC-UC1a-03b)

scenarios.title: Default — no controls overlay before the first tap
preconditions: a video or recorded live stream is actively playing on any in-scope surface
the post has just rendered
no tap has occurred yet
steps: Render the actively-playing post without any tap
Assert: NO controls overlay element exists in the view hierarchy / DOM
Assert: only the media surface is visible

expected.success: On first render of an actively-playing video/recorded LS on any in-scope surface, with no tap yet, no controls overlay element exists in the view hierarchy / DOM — only the media surface is visible (baseline default state).
alternative: The controls overlay must NOT be present before any tap — an overlay element rendered pre-interaction is a baseline default-state failure.

scenarios.title: Control interaction resets the 1s idle countdown
scenarios.automation_note: when-stable: the reset timeout constant is tied to the web 3s->1s fix (TC-UC1a-02c); mobile 1s now; prefer fake-timers / Playwright clock
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
the 1s idle countdown is running
steps: Interact with an overlay control (volume / scrubber) at 800ms (before the 1s timeout)
Assert: the countdown restarts — the overlay is still visible past the original 1000ms
Take no further action; Assert: the overlay auto-dismisses 1000ms AFTER the LAST interaction
Assert: playback continues throughout

expected.success: A control interaction at 800ms restarts the 1s idle countdown — the overlay stays visible through the interaction and auto-dismisses only 1000ms after the LAST interaction; playback continues throughout.
alternative: If the overlay dismisses 1000ms after the FIRST reveal — ignoring the later interaction — the countdown-reset failed; the timer must restart on every control interaction, so repeated interactions each less than 1s apart never dismiss the overlay while the user is still interacting (TC-UC1a-02d).

scenarios.title: Pause tap wins the race against the auto-dismiss timer
scenarios.automation_note: fake-timer race at unit/component level — the pause-vs-auto-dismiss race is e2e-untimeable (flaky); do NOT assert wall-clock timing in real-time e2e (TC-UC1a-05d)
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing video / recorded LS
the 1s idle auto-dismiss timer is about to fire (t approx 999ms)
steps: Dispatch a central pause-button tap at ~999ms — the instant the auto-dismiss would fire (fake-timer race)
Assert: the explicit pause WINS — state becomes paused
Assert: the PLAY icon is shown and persists (not swallowed by the expiring timer)
Assert: the overlay dismisses only on a subsequent tap-outside, not from the fired timer

expected.success: When the central pause tap lands at ~999ms as the 1s auto-dismiss is about to fire, the explicit pause wins: the media pauses, the play icon shows and persists (not swallowed by the expiring timer), and the overlay dismisses only on a subsequent tap-outside.
alternative: The expiring 1s timer must not swallow the pause — a race where the overlay auto-dismisses and the paused / play-icon state is lost (or the media stays playing) is the failure mode; a PLAYING overlay would have dismissed on the timer, but once paused the overlay persists (dismisses only via tap-outside).

scenarios.title: Tap during buffering reveals real state, never a false playing icon
scenarios.automation_note: with-mock: force buffering via network throttle / route delay (or a state mock); TC-UC1a-08c mid-play stall is [AI-INFERRED], flake risk -> mock preferred
preconditions: the media is buffering (not yet playing)
buffering is forced via network throttle / route delay or a state mock
steps: Tap the player surface while buffering
Assert: the controls overlay appears
Assert: the central button reflects the REAL state (loading/paused) — NOT a false 'playing' pause-icon
Assert: no crash and no frozen overlay
Release the throttle; Assert: once playback starts the icon updates to the playing state

expected.success: Tapping the player surface while buffering reveals the overlay with the central button reflecting the real state (loading/paused) — never a false 'playing' pause-icon — with no crash and no frozen overlay; once playback starts the icon updates to the playing state.
alternative: [AI-INFERRED] A mid-playback stall (was playing, then the network stalls) must surface an explicit loading/stall state — the viewer is never left on a silent frozen frame (BR-15). Extends AC-10's initial-buffer case to a mid-play stall per BR-15 'any interruption' (TC-UC1a-08c); inject via network manipulation — flake risk, mock preferred.
The central button must never show a false 'playing' pause-icon while the media is buffering — it must reflect the real (loading/paused) state.

scenarios.title: Backgrounded while PLAYING -> OS-paused, playing overlay dismissed on foreground
scenarios.automation_note: Partial (phase-3-1): iOS Detox background/foreground + real-device confirm (simulator differs, Debouncer.swift:17-21 / PlayerControlsVisibility.swift:16); web has no visibilitychange handler -> web is manual
preconditions: iOS
the controls overlay is visible while the media is PLAYING
the app is backgrounded
wall-clock time > 1s passes while backgrounded
steps: Background the app with a playing overlay visible
Wait > 1s (wall clock)
Return the app to the foreground
Assert: the OS paused the media on background and does NOT auto-resume
Assert: the playing overlay is dismissed (its wall-clock 1s idle timer elapsed while backgrounded)
Assert: no stale mid-countdown overlay

expected.success: On returning to the foreground after backgrounding while PLAYING, the OS-paused media does not auto-resume and the playing overlay is dismissed (its wall-clock 1s idle timer elapsed while backgrounded); there is no stale mid-countdown overlay.
alternative: The media must not silently auto-resume on foreground — the OS pause is a terminal action, not an implicit app toggle (BR-10); and no stale mid-countdown overlay may be left frozen on screen.

scenarios.title: Backgrounded while PAUSED -> stays paused, paused overlay persists on foreground
scenarios.automation_note: Partial (phase-3-1): iOS Detox background/foreground + real-device confirm; web has no visibilitychange handler -> web is manual
preconditions: iOS
the controls overlay is visible while the media is PAUSED
the app is backgrounded
the user then returns the app to the foreground
steps: Background the app with a paused overlay visible
Return the app to the foreground
Assert: the media stays paused (OS paused it; no auto-resume)
Assert: the paused overlay PERSISTS (no idle timer to elapse)
Assert: no stale mid-countdown overlay

expected.success: On returning to the foreground after backgrounding while PAUSED, the media stays paused (no auto-resume) and the paused overlay persists (the paused branch has no idle timer to elapse); there is no stale mid-countdown overlay.
alternative: The media must not auto-resume and the paused overlay must not vanish on foreground — the paused branch has no idle timer and the OS pause is terminal (BR-11 + BR-10); no stale mid-countdown overlay.
